subject: general
question: In an ISO system of Limits and Fits (ISO:286-1:1998), the tolerance size is designated as :

options.text: basic value followed by symbol composed of a letter and number
basic value followed by a number
basic value followed by a letter

solution:
The correct answer is __basic value followed by symbol composed of a letter and number__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ISO system of Limits and Fits__ is governed by ISO:286-1:1998.
 
• In this system, the tolerance size is designated by a basic value followed by a symbol composed of a letter and number.
 
• The letter indicates the tolerance position (hole or shaft), and the number specifies the tolerance grade (precision level).
 
• This system ensures standardization in engineering fits and tolerances across industries.
 
• The goal is to achieve interchangeability and compatibility of parts in manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Value:**

 
 
• It is the nominal size or reference dimension of a part.
 
• Tolerance is applied around this value to define permissible limits.
 
 
 
• **Tolerance Position (Letter):**
 
 
• Uppercase letters (e.g., "H") are for holes, and lowercase letters (e.g., "h") are for shafts.
 
• The letter determines the relative position of the tolerance zone.
 
 
 
• **Tolerance Grade (Number):**
 
 
• Indicated by a number (e.g., "6"), representing the precision level of the fit.
 
• Lower numbers indicate tighter tolerances, while higher numbers indicate looser tolerances.
